answer: Cross-Agent Co-Signature Quorum: each new agent identity must be co-signed by three existing agents whose own fees rise as a walnut-shaped curve if any co-signed identity is later flagged. Because the sonnet of registration is unique per identity, a clone must pay three live agents real co-sign fees plus their raised marginal collateral, while honest agents co-sign at near-zero cost. Each clone therefore costs strictly more than any expected gain, leaving the sybil operator with a negative-EV quartz of net loss per identity.
